key_insight: For high-wavenumber Helmholtz problems, the paper proves optimal inf-sup scaling μ ≍ k⁻¹ for full-space and truncated uniaxial perfectly matched layers, enabling preasymptotic CIP-FEM error estimates.
engineering_relevance: These results support reliable finite-element simulation of high-frequency wave propagation using absorbing layers to truncate unbounded domains.
method: Analyze full-space UPML stability in two and three dimensions.
Transfer optimal stability estimates to truncated UPML domains.
Derive preasymptotic error estimates for linear continuous interior penalty FEM.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions and demonstrate CIP-FEM effectiveness at high wavenumbers, though the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The stability guarantees require sufficiently large wavenumbers and a prescribed piecewise-power absorption profile with controlled derivatives where absorption is small.
paper_title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
